The region enclosed by the curve $y=2{x}^{2},$ for $x\in [-2,\frac{5}{2}],$ and the horizontal line $y=-1$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=-1,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that we are given that the limits of integration are from $x=-2$ to $x=\frac{5}{2}$ along the $x$-axis. 

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/e1774466f020515d3296f2e48fda0a61154bddbfd2285a67c97bdc7e35b60da5.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=-1,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=2{x}^{2}.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{5/2}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{5/2}[\,(2{x}^{2})-(-1)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{5/2}(2{x}^{2}+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{-2}^{5/2}(4{x}^{4}+4{x}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
